blocks.text: 1. Time Steps
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445609380-379341321.png
Sequence Data, the previous topic, established that order genuinely carries meaning. Time Steps take a closer look at the individual positions that make up a sequence, explored throughout this topic.
A time step is one single element, processed at one single point in the sequence's own order, a genuinely foundational unit covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. The Definition
This connects back to order genuinely mattering, already covered in Sequence Data. A time step is genuinely one single position within a sequence, the smallest, most basic unit already covered there.
These are genuinely numbered in order: time step 1, time step 2, and so on, directly matching the ordering already covered as sequence data's own defining property.

blocks.text: 3. Time Steps Versus Epochs
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445609380-790476093.png

A genuinely important terminology distinction connects back to Epochs, already covered in the Training Deep Networks module. An epoch, already covered there, is genuinely one full pass through the training dataset.
A time step, already covered in this topic, is genuinely one position within a single sequence instead, a genuinely different, unrelated concept despite sharing a superficially similar-sounding name.
4. Processing One Time Step At A Time

blocks.alt: Processing One Time Step At A Time
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445609380-940287514.png

This connects back to Sequential Word Generation, already covered in Image Captioning. Sequence Models genuinely process one time step at a time, in genuinely strict order, respecting the order-matters property already covered in Sequence Data.

This is exactly the sequential processing already previewed there, now covered as this module's own core mechanism, the fundamental way every architecture throughout this module handles sequence data.
5. A Preview Of The Hidden State

blocks.alt: A Preview Of The Hidden State
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445609381-676492166.png
A genuinely important, related concept, covered in full in Recurrent Neural Networks, describes how at each time step, the network genuinely carries forward some summary of everything seen so far.

This summary is called a hidden state, a genuinely central idea explored throughout the rest of this module, and the genuinely key mechanism that lets a network remember earlier time steps while processing later ones.

blocks.content: This preview of the hidden state, already covered in this topic, is a genuinely important early exposure to a concept that becomes fully central starting in the very next module, Recurrent Neural Networks.

blocks.text: 6. Recapping Sequence Length

This connects back to the variable-length challenge, already covered in Sequence Data. A sequence's own length genuinely equals its total number of time steps, a genuinely direct, simple relationship.

A genuinely short sequence has few time steps; a genuinely long sequence has many, directly explaining the variable-length challenge already covered in that earlier topic in terms of this topic's own vocabulary.
7. Padding For Sequences
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445609381-177139692.png

This connects back to Padding, already covered in the CNN module. A genuinely related, real practical technique pads shorter sequences with filler time steps, extending the padding idea already covered there to genuinely sequence data.
This lets genuinely different-length sequences be batched together, echoing Padding's own general idea, already covered, of adding extra content to make shapes genuinely consistent.

blocks.text: 8. Time Step Indexing Convention
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445609381-453004831.png
A genuinely important, real practical convention has time steps commonly genuinely indexed starting from either 0 or 1, depending on the specific framework or notation being used.
The genuinely current time step often gets denoted with a subscript, like x sub t, a genuinely standard mathematical notation used consistently throughout the rest of this module.
9. Recognizing Why Understanding Time Steps Genuinely Matters

blocks.alt: Recognizing Why Understanding Time Steps Genuinely Matters
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445609381-98533187.png
This connects back to every architecture covered throughout the rest of this module. Every single one of them genuinely processes sequences time step by time step, already covered in this topic.

Debugging or reasoning about a Sequence Model's own internal behavior is another genuine case where thinking in terms of individual time steps, already covered, makes that reasoning genuinely tractable.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates iterating through a sequence one time step at a time, illustrating the processing order already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
sentence = ["the", "quick", "brown", "fox", "jumps"]

print(f"Sequence length (already covered in this topic): {len(sentence)} time steps")

hidden_state_summary = ""  # a genuinely simplified stand-in for the hidden state already previewed in this topic

for t, word in enumerate(sentence):
    hidden_state_summary += word + " "
    print(f"Time step {t}: processing '{word}', hidden state so far: '{hidden_state_summary.strip()}'")

max_length = 8  # already covered as padding for sequences in this topic
padding_needed = max_length - len(sentence)
padded_sentence = sentence + ["<PAD>"] * padding_needed
print(f"\nPadded sequence to length {max_length} (already covered as padding for sequences in this topic): {padded_sentence}")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows each word processed one time step at a time, with a genuinely simplified summary accumulating across steps, exactly the sequential processing and hidden state preview already covered in this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: A time step is one single position within a sequence.
Time steps are genuinely distinct from epochs, despite the similar-sounding names.
Sequence Models process one time step at a time, in strict order.
A hidden state carries forward a summary of everything seen so far across time steps.
A sequence's length directly equals its total number of time steps.
Padding with filler time steps lets variable-length sequences be batched together.
Time steps are commonly indexed starting from 0 or 1, with the current step denoted like x sub t.
Every architecture covered throughout this module processes sequences time step by time step.
